statement: This is a living disposition map, not a claim that Todoapp replaces focused compiler evidence. Every incomplete application claim states whether useful Todoapp work is planned, a focused compiler fixture is the deliberate owner, or Todoapp is the wrong observer for that contract.

features.claim: Classes, structural API contracts, arrays, iteration, and ordinary runtime values survive both implementation profiles.
Generic and abstract identities and enum-shaped values retain their reviewed type and runtime contracts.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp exercises TodoId, PrettyButtonVariant, requestJson<T>, and the user-visible TodoFilter enum. Generic classes and payload-enum stress cases are clearer and more diagnostic in the focused compiler corpus.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Revisit only when a real Todoapp feature naturally needs a generic class or payload enum, or when an application failure exposes a missing vertical regression.

features.notes: The application evidence is intentionally representative rather than an exhaustive generics or enum matrix.

features.claim: Branches, loops, switches, calls, exceptions, and finally completion preserve Haxe evaluation order in both runtime profiles.

applicationDisposition.rationale: CRUD and UI flows exercise ordinary branches and iteration, and TodoFilter adds one exhaustive domain switch with a both-profile browser oracle. Nested completion, exception/finally behavior, and effect-order traps need smaller deterministic fixtures.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Add application evidence only when a real user workflow depends on a currently focused-only completion or evaluation-order case.

features.notes: The browser truth table proves the domain switch, not every Haxe control-flow form.

features.claim: String and template literal semantics plus Array, Map, iterator, and strict-index behavior remain precise and executable.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp naturally uses strings, interpolation, arrays, and iteration. Adding a Map only to exercise missing-key or strict-index behavior would turn the application into a compiler checklist.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Revisit when an accepted Todo feature genuinely needs keyed dynamic lookup, or when a real app regression needs a vertical Map or index observer.

features.notes: Map presence, nullability, and strict unchecked-index controls remain authoritative in focused fixtures.

features.claim: The opt-in minimal TypeScript runtime omits automatic user-type registration while preserving the admitted application behavior.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp already builds and type-checks the minimal TypeScript variant, but it does not yet start that generated server and observe a real API result.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the disposition when the isolated minimal server passes its Node API transcript and registration-negative control.

features.notes: Minimal TypeScript is a bounded variant, not a third first-class implementation profile.

features.claim: Reflection metadata and embedded resources retain their reviewed target runtime contracts.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Ordinary Todoapp builds expose representative runtime metadata, but synthetic reflection lookups or embedded resources would not improve a Todo workflow and have clearer focused runtime oracles.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Revisit only when an accepted Todoapp capability genuinely resolves a type by name or consumes an embedded Haxe resource.

features.notes: The application is a readability canary for ordinary metadata; reflection and resource differentials remain fixture-owned.

features.claim: Promises, asynchronous callbacks, exceptions, and completion behavior preserve ordering and failure semantics.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Browser and storage paths exercise asynchronous work and catches, while the planned backend expansion still needs deeper server await, error-propagation, and completion behavior.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the backend Bead lands its independent API/runtime failure oracles in both profiles.

features.notes: Browser and storage paths exercise asynchronous work and catches; deep server await/error propagation is a planned backend expansion.

features.claim: Default, named, namespace, aliased, type, and runtime imports retain exact binding identity.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp exercises useful bidirectional default and named imports. Namespace, alias, collision, cycle, and live-binding permutations are more precise and easier to diagnose in the package fixtures.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Revisit when a real application dependency requires a namespace or other currently focused-only import shape.

features.notes: The application proves ordinary interop, not the adversarial ESM binding matrix.

features.claim: Side-effect requests, import attributes, and dynamic request suffixes preserve their explicit module contract.

applicationDisposition.rationale: No current Todoapp behavior needs initialization-only imports, import attributes, or optional module loading. Adding one only to exercise syntax would not create honest application evidence.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Open a separately reviewed application Bead if an accepted optional feature or real dependency requires one of these module contracts.

features.notes: The capabilities remain supported and focused-test-owned; they are only not applicable to the current Todoapp observer.

features.claim: Reviewed module-level functions and ordered module directives emit without synthetic class leakage.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Direct module functions and directive prologues are source-shape and module-contract features, not Todo user behavior. An arbitrary annotation in the app would misrepresent their architecture and proof surface.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Revisit after the dedicated module architecture is settled and only if a genuine Todoapp consumer needs a file-level public function or directive.

features.claim: Haxe null, JavaScript undefined, optional fields, and missing values remain distinguishable where the contract requires it.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp already observes nullable routes, store results, and optional fetch fields. The planned backend contract still needs a natural omitted-field update that proves an unchanged value is preserved.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the backend API suite proves omitted PATCH fields preserve existing state in both profiles.

features.notes: Todoapp uses nullable routes, store results, and optional fetch fields; exact undefined and omitted controls remain focused.

features.claim: Generated TypeScript and classic declarations expose precise closed public contracts to strict consumers.
Haxe source consumes typed authored TypeScript and TSX through reusable extern/import contracts.
features.notes: The authored TypeScript and TSX modules are loaded by the browser bundle, so the Node API smoke is intentionally not counted as runtime evidence for this web-only interop path.

features.claim: Authored TypeScript consumes the active profile's generated Haxe module without cross-profile artifacts.
features.notes: The authored TypeScript consumer is part of the browser bundle; Node validates the server API, not this generated-Haxe-to-TypeScript import boundary.

features.claim: Host globals, native callbacks, extern values, and runtime-guarded bindings use exact typed identities rather than emitted names.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Express, process, fetch, DOM, and React callbacks already cross real host boundaries. The planned backend work will add deeper Node error, persistence, and callback behavior without inventing collision cases in the app.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the backend expansion lands its reviewed host-boundary scenarios in both profiles.

features.notes: Express, process, fetch, DOM, and React callbacks exercise real host boundaries; identity collisions and invalid guarded forms remain focused.

features.claim: One checked HXX intent emits source TSX, low-level TypeScript createElement calls, and classic createElement runtime behavior.

applicationDisposition.rationale: The application covers the core markup path, while the dedicated HXX work owns the remaining stable positive syntax, component, accessibility, and visual application cases.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the HXX expansion lands its bounded both-profile browser and generated-source evidence.

features.notes: The application covers the core markup path; the dedicated HXX expansion owns the complete stable positive matrix and visual polish.

features.claim: Typed hooks, events, Router components, navigation, and route parameters work in the maintained browser application.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Hooks, events, navigation, and route parameters already run in the application, but the dedicated HXX expansion still owns the accepted breadth and accessibility work.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the HXX expansion's reviewed browser scenarios and source-shape checks land.

features.claim: Runtime DCE, declaration reachability, and explicitly reusable library surfaces remain separate contracts.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp already proves one real authored-TypeScript-to-generated-Haxe retention boundary under full DCE. Arbitrary reusable-library and declaration reachability graphs are not application behaviors.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Add another application canary only when a real Todoapp integration exposes a distinct reachability failure.

features.notes: Todoapp builds with full DCE and keeps one authored-TS export; the reusable-library graph remains deliberately fixture-owned.

features.claim: Generated locals, imports, module functions, helpers, and user declarations receive deterministic collision-safe names.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Ordinary application names provide a readability canary, while deliberately colliding declarations, aliases, helpers, and module functions would make the Todoapp less understandable without improving user behavior.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Retain an application regression only when a naturally chosen app name exposes a compiler collision; keep the full matrix focused.

features.notes: Ordinary application naming is exercised; adversarial same-name declarations and binding collisions remain focused.

features.claim: Representative generated tokens and runtime stack stages retain exact Haxe source provenance.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Todoapp publishes map files, but it does not yet resolve reviewed generated tokens back to exact authored Haxe positions. File existence alone cannot prove source provenance.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the dedicated map owner passes exact path, line, column, portability, and determinism assertions.

features.notes: Todoapp publishes maps, but exact application token and stack assertions remain to be added.

features.claim: Warm compiler-server requests remain equivalent to isolated fresh builds across relevant profile and configuration changes.

applicationDisposition.rationale: The compiler-server fixture proves request reuse in isolation, while the Todoapp performance work still needs a bounded warm-build comparison for the flagship application.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when reviewed cold, warm, and no-op Todoapp measurements are recorded without replacing the focused lifecycle owner.

features.claim: A failed generation preserves the complete last-good owned tree and publishes no partial source, declaration, map, support, or manifest artifacts.

applicationDisposition.rationale: The focused transaction suite injects failures precisely, but the flagship application still needs one representative last-good build, failure, repair, and recovery journey.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim when the Todoapp rollback Bead proves the public tree remains byte-identical through a failed rebuild in both profiles.

features.notes: The focused failure-injection owner remains authoritative. Dedicated live child Bead genes-1x1g.8 owns the representative Todoapp last-good workflow and will enter the tracked roadmap through the required post-merge export PR.

features.claim: Generated trees remain deterministic and reviewed structural or timing costs do not regress silently.

applicationDisposition.rationale: Checked snapshots expose source drift, but the application does not yet have reviewed structural budgets or stable timing evidence for both profiles.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Complete the application claim after same-run measurements justify deterministic ceilings and any noisy timings receive an explicit report-only or blocking disposition.

features.notes: Todoapp snapshots detect source drift; application structural and latency budgets are not yet reviewed.

features.claim: The bounded TypeScript-to-Haxe migration subset is proven independently from Haxe-to-Genes compiler conformance.

applicationDisposition.rationale: ts2hx translates a bounded TypeScript implementation subset into Haxe. Its correctness cannot be inferred from the flagship Haxe-to-Genes application, so it retains an independent test and product claim.
applicationDisposition.revisitTrigger: Revisit only if a separately designed migration example executes a real translated application without counting that result as Haxe-to-Genes compiler conformance.

features.notes: The historical Todoapp PRD proposed a roundtrip, but current product policy keeps ts2hx evidence separate from the flagship Haxe application.
